past_actions.summary: Schedule a meeting with branch manager to formally flag the sustained 50% application volume decline and request a portfolio diversification conversation — specifically, cross-training or reassignment to support mortgage or small business lending.
past_actions.emotional_state: Controlled concern. Not panicking — panic is expensive — but the low-grade alarm is there. I sleep fine but I'm thinking about this more than I'd like. The feeling isn't dread, it's more like the feeling you get when you realize the weather is changing and you're still deciding whether to grab a jacket. You're not wet yet. You're not going to be wet if you move now.

past_actions.summary: Block 90 minutes daily on calendar for mortgage underwriting and SBA 7(a)/504 loan training. Contact the regional training coordinator to formally enroll in the next available NMLS-approved mortgage origination course. Request access to the bank's internal SBA loan files from the past two years to self-study deal structures. Set a 30-day milestone: complete modules 1-4 of mortgage origination curriculum and shadow at least two live mortgage closings.
past_actions.emotional_state: Grounded. The confirmation of what I already suspected is not frightening — it is clarifying. I feel the kind of calm that comes from having moved first. There is a small undertow of pressure knowing that the institutional gears are now turning above me and timelines may compress, but that pressure is productive. I am not in denial, I am not catastrophizing. I am a 44-year-old professional who has done this work for two decades and still has runway, savings, a supportive manager, and a bank that needs people who can do more than one thing. The next 60 days matter. I will make them count.

past_actions.summary: Apply today for Maria Santos's $2,500 retraining grant through the council program. The NMLS mortgage origination course costs approximately $300-600 depending on employer reimbursement status. The grant covers this and potentially additional SBA certification costs. Complete the application form, attach proof of enrollment in the NMLS-approved course, and submit before end of business. This is a no-downside action — the grant is available, Kevin is eligible, the application takes two hours, and it offsets real out-of-pocket training costs.
past_actions.emotional_state: Focused and slightly accelerated. The calm from tick 1 is still the foundation, but the word-of-mouth about David's memo introduces a new variable: institutional timelines are now outside my direct control in a way they were not before. That is not alarming — it is information. The right response is compression, not panic. I am moving the closing shadow up, filing the grant today, and making sure David sees my progress before Sandra does. This is still methodical. It is methodical with a tighter clock.

past_actions.summary: Formally accept David Chen's structured NMLS mortgage licensing pathway. Send written acknowledgment to David confirming: acceptance of the 8-month timeline, intent to use tuition reimbursement for the NMLS-approved course, readiness to begin co-originator exposure on live mortgage files as soon as David can schedule it. Request a formal first check-in at the 30-day mark. This locks in the institutional commitment from both sides and signals to David — and anyone watching — that Kevin is a reliable investment, not a flight risk.

Prepare a written one-page brief for David Chen's formal 30-minute check-in: document the early delinquency patterns I have observed firsthand on auto loans processed in the last 60 days, note the 18% application volume decline I am seeing on the front end, and confirm NMLS module completion progress (modules 1-3 complete, modules 4-6 on schedule). Bring this brief to the meeting as a tangible deliverable — not a presentation, just one page showing I have been paying attention to the same data David is sharing upward. Ask David directly what the new written underwriting criteria will look like and request a draft copy so I can align my intake workflow before it is formally published.

Formally request a portfolio expansion meeting with David Chen (or his successor/interim manager if David has departed) to add small business lending and personal loan origination to Kevin's active scope. The NMLS mortgage pathway is 8 months out. Small business and personal loan work is something Kevin can do with existing credentials now. Frame it as: auto volume is structurally declining, Kevin has the compliance and credit skills, the bank has SBA products and personal loan products that are underutilized, and Kevin wants to be the originator who covers that gap starting this month. This is not a request for reassignment — it is a request to expand the current role rather than wait for attrition to force a move.

Process Amir Patel's $12,000 EV charger loan application as the first concrete proof-of-concept for the portfolio expansion. Follow up with Betty Kowalski on the tick 8 outreach — genuine check-in, no product push. Respond to David Chen's informal debrief request with real intelligence from the community center session. Hold the second Community Center financial office hours session with a new agenda item on gig-economy small business loan options. Continue NMLS modules 5-6 and confirm HR paperwork status with interim management.

Process Amir Patel's $12,000 EV charger capital improvement loan application. Pull his file from the tick 5 term sheet meeting, confirm loan parameters: $12,000 principal, standard commercial improvement rate, 60-month term. Run credit and business cash flow review. Prepare the application package for underwriting and advance it through the bank's formal loan processing pipeline. This is a small business loan origination under Kevin's expanded scope request — treating it as the first concrete proof-of-concept for the portfolio expansion. Communicate clearly to Amir on timeline and next steps.

Identify and make direct contact with whoever has assumed David Chen's management responsibilities — by name, not by title — and get a definitive answer on the portfolio expansion request submitted at tick 8. I walk to their office or schedule a 15-minute meeting this week. My question is specific: has the request to add small business and personal loan origination to my active scope been reviewed, and if so, what is the decision? If it has not been reviewed, I request a 30-minute meeting to present the case directly, using the Amir Patel EV charger loan as the primary evidence: here is a real $12,000 small business loan I originated under existing credentials in a sector where auto loan volume has dropped 21%. This is what portfolio diversification looks like in practice. I do not wait for institutional gears to turn on their own timeline anymore.

past_outcomes.action: Forced decision meeting with interim bank management on portfolio expansion; Amir Patel loan cleared underwriting; NMLS advanced to 30%; contingency plan formalized
past_outcomes.narrative: Kevin walked into the interim manager Sandra Briggs's office with the one-pager and refused 'we are still reviewing it' as an answer for the third consecutive tick — she gave him a concrete date: a formal decision by the end of next week. The Amir Patel $12,000 EV charger loan cleared underwriting with a conditional approval, pending one additional piece of business cash flow documentation that Kevin communicated to Amir within the same day. David Chen responded to Kevin's message with the name of the right person to own the portfolio expansion decision (confirming it is Sandra), which validated the approach Kevin took. NMLS progress advanced to 30% with module 7 now logged, and Kevin wrote down his tick 13 contingency threshold — two regional credit unions and one regional bank identified as external targets if the internal path closes.

reflections.reflection: Six ticks in and I am still employed, still in the retraining pipeline, still burning savings at a rate that is manageable but not comfortable. The word-of-mouth about David is the most destabilizing signal I have received so far — not because I know what it means, but because I don't. Every structural move I have made since tick 0 has been anchored to David Chen's sponsorship of my NMLS pathway. If that sponsorship walks out the door with him, I have a tuition reimbursement form and a training log that lives only on my personal calendar. That is not enough. I should have filed the HR paperwork two ticks ago. I did not. I kept treating the verbal agreement as sufficient because David had been reliable and I did not want to look like I was hedging against him. That was a mistake.
reflections.identity_shift: I am beginning to separate my professional identity from the bank as an institution and reattach it to the skills I am building. For the first decade of my career I was 'a loan officer at First Community Bank.' Now I am increasingly thinking of myself as someone who understands credit, risk, and financial access — and who happens to currently work at a bank. That shift is subtle but it matters. It means the NMLS license is not just a hedge against one role disappearing. It is the foundation of something portable.
regrets: Did not file the NMLS co-originator paperwork with HR in ticks 4 or 5 — left the institutional commitment floating on David's personal goodwill rather than making it structural.

Waited too long to make myself visible to community stakeholders like Lisa Freeman. There was an obvious opportunity to be the human face of bank lending products for the retraining pipeline and I did not move on it until now.
successes: Delivered the tick 5 brief to David — concrete, data-grounded, showed I was watching the same metrics he was reporting upward. That was the right move regardless of what happens to David's role.
NMLS modules 1-3 complete and on schedule. The 90-minute daily block has held for five ticks. That is real.

Identified and acted on the Lisa Freeman outreach opportunity this tick before it became irrelevant. Positioning myself as the operational link between bank products and retraining enrollees creates value that any manager would recognize.
reflections.adaptation_notes: Primary risk this tick: manager-level instability threatening the institutional NMLS pathway. Mitigation: formalize through HR immediately, make the paperwork independent of any single person. Secondary opportunity: the community retraining pipeline needs someone with financial product knowledge who can sit in a room and answer questions. I am that person. Monthly office hours at the Community Center is low-cost, high-visibility, and directly responsive to what Lisa Freeman has been built toward. If David is gone and I need a new manager to see my value, being the banker who shows up at the Community Center is the kind of story that travels. Financial note: at current burn rate I have approximately 6-7 months of runway. The training pathway must produce a concrete role change before month 8 or the math stops working.

reflections.reflection: Nine ticks in. The savings burn accelerated sharply at tick 8 — $3,122 in a single month against my usual $2,500-$2,700 baseline. That is a warning number. I am now looking at roughly $26,000 in savings, a monthly deficit of approximately $3,100 at recent pace, and a skill-relevance gap that is still at 0.65. My NMLS runway is 8 months from the pathway start, which means the credential arrives around tick 12 or 13. The math is tighter than it was. What has actually changed between tick 6 and tick 9, though, is real: the HR paperwork is in the system, the community center office hours are established, Amir Patel has submitted a live loan application that I can originate under my existing credentials, and I made the formal case for portfolio expansion last tick. Those are not hollow actions. They are structural moves that change what I can do and what I look like to anyone evaluating my position.
reflections.identity_shift: At tick 6 I noticed I was starting to separate my professional identity from the bank and reattach it to my skills. At tick 9 that shift has advanced further. I no longer think of myself primarily as an auto loan officer who is retraining. I think of myself as a community-facing lending professional who happens to still have an auto loan originator title. The Amir Patel EV charger loan is the clearest evidence of that shift — six months ago I would not have seen a commercial property improvement loan as mine to originate. Now it feels like the obvious next move. That is an identity change, not just a skill addition.
regrets: The tick 8 burn of $3,122 is still not fully explained to me. I need to understand what drove it — whether it was administrative costs related to the portfolio expansion meeting request, or whether the savings figure in state.json is absorbing some baseline deficit I have been underestimating. I have been modeling my monthly deficit as roughly $2,571 from routine expenses but actual burn is running higher. I should have caught this pattern earlier.

I have not yet made explicit contact with whoever has taken over David Chen's management responsibilities at the bank. The portfolio expansion request went to 'David Chen or his successor' but I do not know with certainty who that successor is. That ambiguity is a risk — the request may be sitting in a handoff gap. I should have resolved this at tick 8 rather than filing the request against an uncertain target.
successes: Community Center office hours are live. First session had 3 attendees. One left knowing about a specific credit product they did not know existed. That is a real outcome — not a metric, a person.

Amir Patel activated a $12,000 EV charger loan application. This is the first small business loan I am originating outside the auto context. It is proof-of-concept for the portfolio expansion case and it is a real transaction that helps the bank's loan volume in a contracting market.

David Chen maintaining informal contact with me after his departure is a strong signal about my professional positioning. He is not maintaining contact with the bank — he is maintaining contact with me specifically. That relationship has value that does not appear on any spreadsheet.
Filed the NMLS HR paperwork at tick 7 and confirmed it. The pathway is now institutionally documented and does not depend on any single manager's memory or goodwill.
reflections.adaptation_notes: The key tension right now is between pace and sustainability. The environment is deteriorating faster than my NMLS retraining timeline. Employment at 67%, consumer spending at 40% of baseline, protests at 9 incidents — this is not a soft landing. The portfolio expansion to small business and personal loans is the right bridge strategy, but it is not confirmed yet. I need to treat the Amir Patel origination as urgent evidence, not a leisurely process. On savings: I need to get tighter on my monthly expense monitoring. The $3,122 tick 8 burn cannot become the new baseline or my runway compresses to under 9 months. I do not need to cut the training — that would be a false economy — but I need to understand where the money is actually going. Financial note: effective savings approximately $26,000. At $3,000/month burn, roughly 8.5 months of runway. NMLS credential ETA 3-4 months from now. The windows are converging. I need the portfolio expansion approved or a role change signal from management before month 12 or the options narrow sharply.
